subject: Commercial proposal: committed node-hour bundle + partner uplift allocation
messages:
From: Maya R. <maya.r@acme-systems.com>
To: priya.n@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-systems.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial inquiry: committed node-hour bundle for data platform

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. Acme is preparing a procurement packet for a year-long committed node-hour purchase to run our analytics/embedding workloads. We want a firm list price for a 12-month commit (estimated 2.2M node-hours), bundled with a 3-month onboarding credit and an optional monitoring add-on.

Two questions up front:
- Can Redwood show the partner uplift allocation (we're working with CloudBroker to manage the engagement)? They need to appear on the commercial waterfall so our legal and finance teams can reconcile commissions.
- Will Redwood accept CloudBroker on the invoice or should we route invoicing to CloudBroker separately? Acme prefers a single invoice to simplify purchase order matching.

If you prefer, share a term sheet and I'll loop in procurement for a fast review. We're targeting a signed PO by mid-June.

Best,
Maya R.
Head of Cloud Procurement
Acme Systems

Attachment: none

From: priya.n@redwood.com <priya.n@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya.r@acme-systems.com>
Cc: ben.c@redwood.com, laura.b@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial inquiry: committed node-hour bundle for data platform

Maya — thanks, super helpful context.

Attached is a concise term sheet and SKU mapping worksheet that reflects a committed 12-month node-hour bundle at a tiered unit price (volume-based steps). Highlights:
- Committed quantity: 2,200,000 node-hours (12 months)
- List-price anchoring with two volume tiers (first 1.0M / next 1.2M) to keep unit economics predictable
- One-time onboarding credit: USD 60,000 applied as a negative invoice line in month 1 (we can make this a credit memo if you prefer)
- Optional monitoring add-on at fixed per-node-hour rate, billed monthly if enabled

Regarding partner uplift / commission handling:
- Redwood can provide a waterfall in the term sheet showing a 7% partner enablement allocation (of net ARR) to CloudBroker.
- For invoicing, we can issue a single invoice to Acme and include a partner routing line in our internal ERP; however Redwood prefers to pay partners separately rather than listing them as invoice payees on the customer invoice. That said, we can discuss a passthrough invoice to CloudBroker if Acme needs them visible on the PO.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll mark this term sheet as draft and suggest Ben (channel) and Laura (finance) review routing/contract language.
2) If Acme confirms the preferred invoice flow, we'll update the commercial language and produce an updated term sheet for procurement.

Uploading: Redwood_Commercial_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf, SKU_nodehour_mapping.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to run through the waterfall.

— Priya Natarajan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

priya.n@redwood.com

Hi Priya / Ben — thanks for the draft term sheet. Procurement had two clarifying asks after a quick pass: 

1) Invoice flow: Acme strongly prefers Redwood to put CloudBroker on the invoice (so we can route partner fees to their ledger line). If Redwood cannot be listed as a co-payee, procurement needs a short note accepting that Redwood will collect and remit to CloudBroker and we will accept that routing for this PO.

2) Partner enablement mechanics: Procurement wants the partner allocation to be a visible line item on the invoice (non-invoiced pass-through is OK only if CloudBroker signs a SOW directly with Acme). Can CloudBroker accept a SOW with Acme instead? Bob, can you confirm CloudBroker's preference?

3) SKU parity: our legal requests confirmation that the SKU_nodehour_mapping.xlsx will be part of the SOW/attachment so we can tie metering to billed units.

We have a procurement review meeting on Thursday; if we can get confirmation on the invoice mechanics and the revised term sheet by Wednesday EOD, we'll be able to move to PO issuance quickly.

Thanks,
Maya

Maya / Bob — thanks for the clear asks. Quick internal summary and a proposed path so procurement can close the PO on Thursday: 

Internal notes (Ben / Laura):
- Redwood can show a partner allocation line on the commercial waterfall in the term sheet (we've done this for other customers). We propose the following wording on the customer invoice: "Partner enablement allocation (remitted separately) — 7% of net ARR" displayed as an informational line only; Redwood will remain the invoiced party to Acme.
- If Acme requires CloudBroker to appear as a payee on the customer invoice, Redwood's standard approach is to request a partner passthrough arrangement. That requires a contract amendment and our finance team (Laura) to approve routing/payout terms. Likely a 5-business-day processing window for passthrough setup.

Proposal to close the gap quickly: 
1) Redwood issues a revised term sheet (attached) with an explicit waterfall showing the 7% partner allocation as an informational invoice line and the SKU mapping embedded as an annex.
2) CloudBroker (Bob) to confirm if they will accept a standalone SOW with Acme; if yes, Acme can route the partner fees via the SOW and Redwood will invoice the net amount. If CloudBroker prefers invoice visibility on the customer invoice, Ben/Laura will start the passthrough setup (5 business days).
3) Redwood will convert the one-time onboarding credit to a credit memo in month 1 (preferred by Acme's AP team).

Action items: 
- Maya: confirm whether Acme will accept an informational partner line (Redwood remits to CloudBroker) or requires CloudBroker on the invoice itself.
- Bob: confirm SOW preference.
- Ben/Laura: please confirm if passthrough setup is feasible if required (cc'd).

I'll attach the revised term sheet now and mark it "Procurement draft". If Acme confirms the informational line is acceptable by Wednesday EOD, we'll finalize and route the PO. If not, we'll initiate passthrough and share ETA.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call this afternoon to clear any remaining items.

— Priya Natarajan
